newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rate pares gains on demand at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rate pares gains on demand at close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates pared early gains to close 45 basis points up at 23.45 percent due to late demand, traders said.

"There were people with cash who had to pay what they were offered to cover positions at the close, probably in advance of the cutoff for checking accounts," said a floor trader, referring to Wednesday's cutoff date for banks settling outstanding balances with the central bank.

The cutoff date tends to cause liquidity shortages in the secondary money market and forces rates up. Heavier volume in late trade brought the overnight Cetes rate down from an average of about 24 percent for the session, traders said.
For most of the session, rates were pressured by expectations of rate hikes at Tuesday evening's primary Cetes auction and gains in U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rates.
A survey of traders by Reuters showed they expected the benchmark 28-day Cetes rate to rise an average of 120 basis points to 24.58 percent at the auction.
Secondary 28-day Cetes and bank rates closed at 26 percent and 29 percent, respectively.
Banco de Mexico injected 4.185 billion pesos into the secondary market though credit auctions on Tuesday to offset liquidity shortfalls.
Traders estimated a liquidity shortfall of 4.3 billion pesos on Wednesday.
